chunks.title: Define full-stack scope without claiming equal depth
chunks.text: State the candidate's strongest layer, the complementary layer they can deliver, and the kinds of products shipped end to end. Support breadth with one outcome spanning interface, API, data, or deployment. Avoid implying expert-level depth across every technology unless the experience section genuinely demonstrates it.

chunks.title: Make a broad full-stack skill set scannable
chunks.text: Group skills into Frontend, Backend, Data, Testing, and Cloud or DevOps. Within each group, lead with the technologies most relevant to the job and used in recent work. Avoid one alphabetized list because it obscures depth, layer ownership, and how the candidate assembles a complete application.

chunks.title: Show end-to-end ownership in project descriptions
chunks.text: Describe the user workflow, client implementation, API behavior, data model, authentication or authorization, and deployment path that the candidate personally built. Select the most important architectural choices rather than enumerating every package. Add a measured usage, quality, or delivery result where evidence exists.

chunks.title: Describe the end-to-end request lifecycle
chunks.text: A concise full-stack architecture statement can follow one important request from browser interaction through state handling, API validation, business logic, persistence, and response rendering. Mention deployment or background processing when relevant. Explain one boundary or trade-off, such as server-side validation, caching, or optimistic updates.

chunks.title: Replace a stack list with an end-to-end result
chunks.text: Weak: 'Created a React, Node, and MongoDB application.' Strong: 'Delivered a React booking flow backed by validated Express endpoints and MongoDB availability checks, preventing duplicate reservations during concurrent submissions.' The stronger bullet explains how the layers cooperate and what product risk the implementation addressed.

chunks.title: Balance frontend and backend keyword coverage
chunks.text: Relevant terms may span responsive interfaces, component architecture, state management, REST or GraphQL APIs, authentication, data modeling, testing, CI/CD, containers, and cloud deployment. Weight the vocabulary toward the vacancy's actual emphasis and connect important terms to evidence rather than forcing equal coverage of every layer.
